findings.title: .env file is publicly downloadable
findings.description: Your .env usually holds database passwords and API keys.
findings.evidence: HTTP 200, 293 bytes; variables: SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY
findings.remediation: Remove .env from the public/ or dist/ folder, add it to .gitignore, and rotate every secret it contained.

findings.title: OpenAI API key in /.env
findings.description: Anyone visiting the site can copy this key and run up your OpenAI bill.
findings.remediation: Revoke the key at platform.openai.com, move OpenAI calls to a server/edge function, read the key from a server-side env var.

findings.title: OpenAI API key in client code
findings.description: Anyone visiting the site can copy this key and run up your OpenAI bill.
findings.remediation: Revoke the key at platform.openai.com, move OpenAI calls to a server/edge function, read the key from a server-side env var.

findings.title: Supabase service_role key in /.env
findings.description: The service_role key bypasses Row Level Security: anyone can read, change or delete every row.
findings.remediation: Rotate the JWT secret / service key in Supabase now, use only the anon key in the browser, and do privileged work in an Edge Function.

findings.title: Supabase service_role key in client code
findings.description: The service_role key bypasses Row Level Security: anyone can read, change or delete every row.
findings.remediation: Rotate the JWT secret / service key in Supabase now, use only the anon key in the browser, and do privileged work in an Edge Function.

findings.title: CORS reflects any origin with credentials
findings.description: Any website can make logged-in requests to your app and read the responses.
findings.evidence: Origin: https://achilles-cors-probe.example -> ACAO: https://achilles-cors-probe.example, ACAC: true
findings.remediation: Only allow your own front-end origin(s); never echo the Origin header back.

findings.title: .git folder is publicly downloadable
findings.description: Attackers can rebuild your full source code and history, including old secrets.
findings.remediation: Block /.git in your web server or stop deploying the .git directory.

findings.title: Session cookie 'session_id' missing HttpOnly
findings.description: Session cookies without HttpOnly can be stolen by XSS; without Secure they leak over HTTP.

findings.title: Site is served over plain HTTP
findings.description: Logins and data travel unencrypted.
findings.remediation: Serve the site over HTTPS and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

findings.title: JavaScript source maps are public
findings.description: Source maps hand out your original, readable source code (comments included).
findings.remediation: Disable production source maps (e.g. `build.sourcemap: false` in Vite, `productionBrowserSourceMaps: false` in Next.js).

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy
findings.description: Without CSP, any XSS bug can load scripts from anywhere and steal sessions.

findings.title: Page can be framed (clickjacking)
findings.description: Another site can embed your app in an invisible frame and trick users into clicking.

findings.title: Alternate HTTP port 8000 open
findings.description: Often a dev server (Django/uvicorn) or admin panel.
findings.remediation: Close port 8000 in your firewall / cloud security group, or bind the service to 127.0.0.1 or a private network. Only 80/443 should face the internet.

findings.title: Unexpected open port 8443 (https-alt)
findings.description: A service other than the website is reachable from the internet.
findings.remediation: If this service isn't meant to be public, firewall it.

findings.title: Supabase anon key in client code
findings.description: Normal and public by design, but it means your data is only as safe as your Row Level Security policies.
findings.remediation: Make sure RLS is enabled on every table in Supabase > Authentication > Policies.

findings.title: Missing Referrer-Policy
findings.description: Full URLs (with tokens in them) may leak to other sites.

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options
findings.description: Browsers may MIME-sniff responses.

findings.title: Server header reveals version
findings.description: Version numbers help attackers pick exploits.
findings.remediation: Remove or genericize the server header.

findings.title: X-Powered-By header reveals version
findings.description: Version numbers help attackers pick exploits.
findings.remediation: Remove or genericize the x-powered-by header.

findings.title: Web port 8088 open (radan-http)
findings.description: Expected for a web app.

findings.description: Detected technology. Used to choose which checks matter.
